summary: Transparent egress proxy header rewriting truncates TLS SNI during CONNECT, causing presigned S3 artifact fetches to fail intermittently
summary_detail: FinEdge private deployment started seeing intermittent 403 and TLS certificate name mismatch errors when Redwood serving nodes attempted to fetch model artifacts via presigned S3 URLs. Failures began after customer rolled a global HTTP CONNECT header rewrite policy on their egress proxy appliance.
description:
Issue summary:
- Symptoms: Artifact download failures (403) and sporadic TLS errors (presenting default cert / certificate name mismatch) from serving nodes during model pulls. Failures affect a subset of nodes and are intermittent across retries.
- Impact: Model pulls for autoplay model group fail ~10-20% of attempts, causing container start delays and degraded autoscaling behaviour for FinEdge's private deployment.
- Suspected root area: Egress proxy transparent rewrite of CONNECT payloads/header transformations interfering with TLS ClientHello SNI extension when combined with large X-Forwarded-For header insertions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private agent in customer VPC behind their transparent egress proxy (policy: add X-Forwarded-For and inject an internal correlation header on CONNECT).
2) Trigger model pull via Redwood private control plane (model size ~1.2GB) which uses presigned S3 URL with long query string.
3) Observe intermittent handshake failures in serving node logs and 403s from S3 presigned URL on retries.
4) Capture packet trace on serving node (tcpdump) during failed handshake to inspect ClientHello and TCP segments.
observed_logs: serving_node[2026-03-10T14:12:08Z] ERROR artifact_fetch - TLS handshake failed: server returned certificate for 's3.amazonaws.com' but request host was 's3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com'
control-plane: model_pull: node 7ac3 failed to download artifact (attempt 1/3) - connection reset by peer
pcap_findings: Packet capture shows TLS ClientHello split across two TCP segments during CONNECT tunnel establishment when proxy inserted correlation header (total CONNECT payload > 1.6KB).

Second segment contains the end of the ClientHello TLS extension block; when proxy performs in-line header rewrite it drops/truncates final 40-120 bytes of the TLS extensions in ~17% of observed sessions, removing SNI or truncating host name bytes.

When SNI is clipped the origin returns a default cert which triggers certificate name mismatch in the client and subsequent retries occasionally generate 403 due to changed Host header semantics at proxy termination.
investigation_notes: 03/10 15:10 - Support replicated failing model pull in staging with customer's proxy policy (thanks to SE Jake Brooks for test harness).
03/10 16:05 - Packet-level diff between successful and failed flows shows consistent truncation of TLS extension tail only when proxy injects >640B of extra headers into CONNECT payload.
03/10 17:30 - Reproduced with curl using CONNECT through proxy: curl --proxy CONNECT ... reproduces certificate mismatch when payload crosses size threshold.

03/11 09:12 - Customer proxy vendor (NetEdge) confirmed a documented bug in firmware 6.1.x where inline HTTP CONNECT modification can corrupt subsequent tunneled TLS payloads under certain buffer flush conditions (internal ticket NET-4521).
03/11 11:00 - Temporary mitigation tested: adding an egress-bypass rule for *.s3.amazonaws.com restored successful artifact pulls for affected nodes in our test.
impact_estimate: Approximately 12-22% of artifact pulls for FinEdge private deployment fail and need retry; end-user latency increases during scale-up events and some pods fail readiness probes leading to transient capacity pressure.
workaround: Customer added an explicit egress bypass for S3 presigned endpoints and removed the global CONNECT header rewrite for requests to S3. This reduced failures to <1% in their canary group.
resolution_plan:
Short term: advise customer to keep bypass rule for S3 endpoints and to disable CONNECT payload rewriting for artifact destinations.
Medium term: customer to upgrade NetEdge proxy to firmware 6.2.1 where NET-4521 is fixed.
Support action: add guidance to Redwood private deploy runbook about egress appliance behaviours that can corrupt tunneled TLS and recommended bypass rules for presigned artifact hosts.
resolution_notes:
03/12 08:20 - Customer upgraded NetEdge to 6.2.1 in canary VPC and tested artifact pulls successfully across 1,000 runs.
03/12 09:00 - Customer rolled upgrade to remaining subnets; monitoring shows artifact fetch success >99.9%.
Ticket status: awaiting customer confirmation on keeping bypass rule removal; Support will follow up in 7 days to close.

2) Create monitoring alert in Console to surface rising artifact fetch 5xx/403 rates per-customer (owner: Observability team).
3) Publish KB article for customers describing proxy behaviors that require egress bypass for presigned URLs and recommended ip/host granular rules.
